**The Weaver of Dawn**

In the time before time, darkness blanketed the world endlessly. The people huddled in caves, knowing only cold and shadow.

High in the mountains lived an old weaver named Ayana, whose fingers had grown stiff with age. One night, she dreamed of colors she had never seen—gold, crimson, and violet dancing together. When she woke, she wept, for such beauty existed only in sleep.

But her granddaughter Maya said, "Grandmother, if you can dream it, perhaps you can weave it."

Ayana's hands trembled as she began. She wove for seven days and seven nights, threading together every hope, every whispered prayer of her people. Her fingers bled, staining the fabric red. Her tears fell, adding silver threads. Her breath, her very life, went into the cloth.

On the eighth morning, Ayana hung her tapestry upon the highest peak. As the wind caught it, the fabric blazed with light—the world's first sunrise.

Ayana closed her eyes for the final time, but her granddaughter continued her work. Each evening, Maya weaves the sunset. Each dawn, she unfurls the morning light.

And so the sky changes colors still, woven by loving hands.
